$comment: Client-bundle budgets, enforced by scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs --check after `pnpm build` in CI; the script header describes the method. Numbers are KB gzip. routeBaselineKbGz is the measured first load of every page (the shared rootMainFiles plus the page's client-reference chunks, each file counted once by content hash), written with --write-baselines; a page fails when it is more than routeDriftAllowanceKbGz over its baseline, and a page without a baseline fails until one is written in the same change. firstLoadP95KbGz and firstLoadMaxKbGz cap the distribution across pages. uniqueClientKbGz caps the distinct client code: every module counted once by its module id, the lazy message catalogs excluded. maxCatalogKbGz holds each catalog, maxRechartsChunks the one shared chart chunk. The summed-chunk aggregate the gate used up to v1.44.0 (3875 KB there, capped at 3900) is still printed but no longer gated: it counted a module once per chunk group it landed in, so it rose whenever a page moved code into on-demand chunks and needed a raise in most releases while no reader downloaded more. Re-based at v1.45.0 from the v1.44.0 build, measured on a local arm64 machine: 110 pages, first load p50 336, p95 437, max 451 KB; unique client code 1904 KB in 1224 modules. The five pages watched before keep their numbers within a kilobyte (/ 359, /measurements 339, /insights/mood 337, /insights 323, /settings/[section] 311), and the metric pages that no watched route covered before are gated now too (/insights/weight 339, /insights/pulse 339). Caps: p95 447 and max 461 KB (10 KB over the measurement), unique client code 1930 KB (about 25 KB, roughly two releases of new client code). A raise or a re-base is a reviewed change with the measured numbers and the reason written here; earlier re-bases are in the history of this file. v1.47.0 raised maxCatalogKbGz from 210 to 250 for the Russian catalog: Cyrillic is two bytes per letter in UTF-8, so the same key set is 1.12 MB raw against about 0.8 MB for the Latin-script locales, 240 KB gz as an emitted chunk where the largest Latin one is under 210. A reader downloads one catalog, once; nothing else in the budget moved. v1.48.0 raised maxCatalogKbGz from 250 to 275: the release adds the seizure diary, the nutrient catalogue and the per-task provider chains to every locale, and the Russian catalog measured 256 KB gz in the CI build (the largest Latin-script one stays under 240). Still one catalog per reader, loaded once. The two new pages got their baselines from the same CI measurement: /seizures 346 and /auth/native-return 289. v1.49.0 raised uniqueClientKbGz from 1930 to 1962: the CI build of the release measured 1937 KB gz in 1331 distinct modules (1224 at the v1.45.0 re-base), four releases of new client code against the two the cap was sized for; the new cap again leaves about 25 KB. The distribution kept falling meanwhile (p95 437 to 386, max 451 to 408 KB). The two new pages got their baselines from the same CI measurement: /emergency-card 332 and /e/[token] 288. Later in 1.49.0 /e/[token] became a route that answers a self-contained document with no client code at all, so its page baseline is gone. The streams that landed after that cap took the CI build of d7a4d19ad to 1965.4 KB gz of distinct client code and the Russian catalog to 282 KB gz, both over their caps. Measured on a local arm64 build against the commit of the 1962 cap (86b9d1a34) with the Turbopack analyzer: plus 34 KB gz of src client code in about sixty modules, none over 1.6 KB gz (the server setup steps, the admin setup-health, notification-health and migrations cards, the relay question, dialog, check and handoff, the medication leaflet section and medicine registry card, the regrouped navigation), no new dependency and no npm package grown, styled-jsx gone (minus 2.7 KB); the catalogs grew by 369 keys and 384 rewritten strings in every locale, none orphaned (i18n-reverse-coverage). Lazy-loading does not lower this number (each module counts once wherever it loads), and the code is the release's own, so 1.49.0 raises uniqueClientKbGz from 1962 to 1990 (about 25 KB over the CI measurement again) and maxCatalogKbGz from 275 to 300 (the largest Latin-script catalog, Polish, measures about 246). The distribution held: p95 391 and max 419 KB locally, against caps of 447 and 461.
